questions.skill: Explain random sampling versus random assignment
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A random sample of 500 adults is surveyed about exercise and sleep; adults who exercise more tend to sleep better. Which conclusion is justified?
questions.prompt_markup: A random sample of 500 adults is surveyed about exercise and sleep; adults who exercise more tend to sleep better. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.text: Exercise causes better sleep for all adults, because the sample was chosen at random.
The association can be generalized to all adults, but it does not show that exercise causes better sleep.
Nothing can be concluded about any adults beyond the 500 who were surveyed.
Exercise causes better sleep, but only for the 500 adults who were surveyed.

questions.correct_answer: The association can be generalized to all adults, but it does not show that exercise causes better sleep.
questions.grading_note: Random sample: generalize. No random assignment: no causation. The others claim causation from a survey, limit the association to the 500 surveyed, or deny any conclusion.

questions.prompt: 60 volunteers are randomly assigned to two diets, and diet A's group loses significantly more weight. Which conclusion is justified?
questions.prompt_markup: 60 volunteers are randomly assigned to two diets, and diet A's group loses significantly more weight. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.text: There is evidence that diet A caused more weight loss for these volunteers, but the result cannot be generalized to all people.
Diet A is associated with weight loss for all people, but the study cannot show that the diet caused it.
Diet A causes more weight loss for all people, because the volunteers were randomly assigned to the two diets.
Nothing can be concluded, because the volunteers chose to participate instead of being randomly sampled.

questions.correct_answer: There is evidence that diet A caused more weight loss for these volunteers, but the result cannot be generalized to all people.
questions.grading_note: Random assignment: evidence of cause for these subjects. No random sample: no generalization. The others generalize to all people, deny causation despite random assignment, or deny any conclusion.

questions.prompt_markup: A random sample of 200 students from a school is randomly assigned to two study methods, and method 1 leads to significantly higher scores. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.text: Method 1 is associated with higher scores, but the study cannot show that it causes them.
There is evidence that method 1 causes higher scores, but only for the 200 students in the study.
There is evidence that method 1 causes higher scores, and the result can be generalized to the school's students.

questions.prompt: Why is a re-randomization test valid only when the original groups were formed by random assignment?
questions.prompt_markup: Why is a re-randomization test valid only when the original groups were formed by random assignment?

choices.text: Without random assignment the group means cannot be computed, so there is nothing to shuffle in the test.
Random assignment makes every difference significant, so the test can only be used after random assignment.
Re-randomization needs exactly the same number of subjects as a fair coin needs flips, so it requires random groups.
The shuffle copies the random assignment; if the groups were not randomly formed, the shuffle does not model how they arose.

questions.correct_answer: The shuffle copies the random assignment; if the groups were not randomly formed, the shuffle does not model how they arose.
questions.grading_note: The simulation models the assignment process. The others are false: group means can always be computed, random assignment does not make results significant, and no coin is involved.
